results.title: The rename: start becomes bay
results.summary: Renamed the `start` verb to `bay` with no alias across the CLI, the command file, the booking, the README and every suite (tasks.md §2.1–2.6): `commands/start.md` moved to `commands/bay.md` via `git mv`, the dispatch entry/usage line/`--bay-dir` help/jsdoc/function/two error strings in `src/cli.js` renamed, `startBay`/`StartResult` renamed to `openBay`/`BayResult`, `bookings/waybill-bay.md` re-pointed at `/waybill:bay` with its pinned assertion, `tests/golden/bay.txt` regenerated (one line changed, no other golden touched), and a new CLI case asserting `start` is now rejected as unknown and absent from usage. Full suite green at 318 pass / 0 fail / 373 TAP ok (baseline 317 / 372); all five boundary and containment acceptance checks pass and `src/inference.js:113`'s deliberately stale comment was left alone per §2.6. — §2 (the rename) is implemented completely and mechanically: `start` → `bay` across the CLI dispatch table, usage block, `--bay-dir` help, error strings, `startBay` → `openBay` and its `StartResult` → `BayResult` typedef, `commands/start.md` → `commands/bay.md`, the booking literal, the README route/command tables, `tests/golden/bay.txt`, and all ~25 call sites in `tests/bay.test.js` — with no `start` residue anywhere in `src/`, `commands/`, `bookings/`, `bin/` or `README.md`. Every mechanical acceptance gate that applies to this phase holds: `src/inference.js`, the six frozen modules, the eight frozen goldens and `no-docket.txt` are all byte-identical to the merge base, the `is not inside a git repository` literal stays out of the `src/cli.js` diff, and §2.6's deliberately stale comment at `src/inference.js:113` was correctly left alone. The one added test (`tests/cli.test.js:306`) pins both halves of the no-alias decision — `start` rejected as unknown and absent from usage. Zero blocking findings; ready to commit once the untracked context map is resolved.
findings: medium/testing tests/commands.test.js:32 — Nothing pins the verb inside a command file's `!` invocation to the CLI dispatch table. If `commands/bay.md:26` had been left invoking `node .../src/cli.js start`, every suite would still be green while the shipped slash command was dead; the same hole covers `bookings/waybill-bay.md`'s `/waybill:bay` literal, which is only pinned incidentally by `tests/inference.test.js:146`. The rename's two user-facing surfaces are therefore unverified end to end → Add an assertion to the commands suite that each `DECLARED` file's `src/cli.js <verb>` invocation resolves to a key of the CLI's `COMMANDS` map, and that each booking's `/waybill:<x>` command has a matching `commands/<x>.md`.

results.title: Rendering: fleet, selection, and the shared cd block
results.summary: Implemented tasks.md §3: added the four golden files (fleet, select, trunk-one-docket, fleet-empty) and wired them into tests/waybill.test.js before writing any renderer, then added renderFleet/renderSelect and the shared cdLines helper to src/waybill.js, widened withFindings to take a plain warnings list, gave renderWaybill an optional IN BAY: block, and pointed src/cli.js's bay() success block at the shared cd helper. Suite went from 318 pass / 373 TAP ok to 338 pass / 397 TAP ok with 0 failures; every boundary criterion (inference zero-diff, six untouched modules, nine pinned goldens, containment) still passes against merge-base 08d0c6f. — Phase §3 (Rendering) is faithfully implemented: the four goldens are byte-identical to the approved design §4 blocks, `withFindings` was widened to a plain warnings list exactly as §3.2 demanded rather than fabricating a synthetic `Inference`, and the `cd` line moved into `cdLines()` with `bay`'s frozen success block left intact per §3.3. I re-ran the contract's boundary checks against the merge-base: `src/inference.js` and the six other guarded modules have zero diff, all nine pre-existing goldens are byte-unchanged, and the `repoRoot` error literal did not ride along — so the guardrails that are the check on the whole approach all hold. Test coverage is genuinely meaningful (padding, pluralisation, warning attribution, block ordering, and a byte-identical no-bay waybill are each asserted separately from the goldens); the three findings are non-blocking polish and this is ready to commit.
findings: medium/testing tests/waybill.test.js:82-108 — the `dockets()` fixture is hand-built and typed only by a JSDoc `@returns {Docket[]}`; the repo has no typecheck script (package.json declares only `test`), so nothing in this phase proves the new renderers accept the shape `fleet()` actually returns. A drift between the fixture and `src/fleet.js`'s `Docket` typedef would stay invisible until §4 wires the CLI → add one case that builds a two-bay repo through `tests/helpers/repo-fixture.js`, passes `fleet(repo)` straight into `renderFleet`, and asserts both branch names appear (assert on rows, not the golden — real branch names cannot match `fleet.txt`).

low/logic src/waybill.js:347 — `renderSelect` calls `docketBlock` unguarded, so an empty fleet yields `Math.max()` === -Infinity and renders a bare `SELECT A DOCKET:` heading over nothing followed by `waybill next <branch>` — the exact shape `renderFleet` guards against one function above (`src/waybill.js:326-327`). Unreachable today because §4.2 will only call it for >1 docket, but the asymmetry is a trap for that task → state the more-than-one-docket precondition in `renderSelect`'s JSDoc, or apply the same guard `renderFleet` uses.

low/pattern-mismatch src/waybill.js:166-168 — `withFindings`'s opening line still reads "Everything both surfaces say about the repository" and the sentence below it still names only `waybill status` and `waybill next`; the helper now serves four renderers, and this file's convention is that the prose explains why at length and stays accurate → update the first paragraph to name the fleet surfaces alongside the two it already lists.

results.title: The exit contract and trunk dispatch
results.summary: Implemented tasks.md §4 (the exit contract and trunk dispatch): `next` now exits 0 iff exactly one waybill was issued — one docket issues its waybill with an `IN BAY:` cd line, zero points at `new`, many print the selection block, both non-zero cases on stdout with exit 2 — plus an optional `next <branch>` positional resolved from the enumerated fleet, a `{error, dockets[]}` shape for `--json` in both non-zero cases, a trunk fleet view for `status`, and the README prose this section falsified. Tests were written first (18 new CLI cases, all failing before implementation); the full suite is 359 pass / 0 fail and all four phase acceptance probes plus every boundary criterion pass. — Phase 3 (tasks.md §4) is implemented faithfully and with unusual care: the exit contract (0 iff exactly one waybill), stdout for both non-zero cases, the optional positional branch, the trunk fleet view, and the non-zero `--json` `{error, dockets[]}` projection all match the spec deltas and the design's verbatim message strings, and the §4.1 constraint was respected — multi-docket repos are built through `tests/helpers/repo-fixture.js` with no new file under `tests/fixtures/`. Containment holds: `src/inference.js` and the six frozen modules are untouched, `src/waybill.js` needed no edit, and the `repoRoot` error string never enters the `src/cli.js` diff (criterion 15). Nothing blocks the commit; the five findings are a stale `status` line in the `--help` usage block, a redundant per-docket leg resolution on the `next <branch>` path, and three low-severity consistency/coverage notes. The test suite was not executed here (reviewer runs read-only), so §7.1's full-suite gate still stands.
findings: medium/spec-deviation src/cli.js:19 — README:99 and the spec's four-verb table (openspec/changes/new-bay-and-fleet/specs/command-surface/spec.md:17, :76-84) now say `status` answers for the docket *or* the repository, but the `--help` USAGE block still reads `status          Where this docket stands, without the waybill`. The `next [<branch>]` line at :18 was updated in the same block, so the help text is internally inconsistent about a behaviour this phase shipped → Update the USAGE line for `status` to name the trunk fleet view (mirroring the README table wording), keeping the column alignment.

medium/performance src/cli.js:189 — `next <branch>` enumerates the whole fleet and, via `fleet()`, runs a full `resolveLeg` per bay (each spawning several git subprocesses plus any booking `stampCmd`, src/bookings.js:247) purely to find one docket by branch name; on the hit path every resolved state is discarded and the chosen docket is then resolved a second time in `issueWaybill` (src/cli.js:91-92). Same double resolution on the single-docket trunk path at :207. `next` is the session inner-loop command, so this is N+1 real subprocess work per invocation → Resolve state lazily for the lookup (find the bay by branch from the worktree records, resolve only the matched docket; keep the full `fleet()` call for the miss path, which genuinely needs the `dockets` projection), or record the accepted cost in the change if `fleet()`'s API is deliberately fixed.

low/logic src/cli.js:189,203 — the fleet listing passes the *operator's* bookings (`resolveBookings(cwd, …)`, :181) into `fleet()`, so each docket's leg in `DOCKETS:`/`SELECT A DOCKET:` is resolved with the trunk's overlay, while `issueWaybill` (:91) deliberately re-resolves from the bay because "a bay carries its own `.waybill/bookings` overlay". A bay with its own overlay can therefore be *listed* at one leg and *issue* a waybill for another → Note the divergence in the change (or resolve each docket with its own bookings) so the listing and the waybill cannot disagree about the same bay; specs/fleet/spec.md:58-62 requires each docket's leg be read "applying the same rules that apply to an operator standing in it".

low/testing tests/cli.test.js:429 — `status` on the trunk is only asserted to raise *no* warnings for a clean fleet; the spec scenario "A docket that cannot be resolved → the warning is reported against that docket's branch" (specs/command-surface/spec.md:94-96) is covered at renderer level only (tests/waybill.test.js:219-226), so nothing end-to-end pins the CLI feeding per-docket warnings through. There is likewise no `status`-inside-a-bay case with other dockets open, the counterpart of the `next` case at :233 → Add one CLI case where a bay resolves with a warning and assert the `<branch>: ` prefix in `status` output, and one asserting `status` inside a bay is unchanged when a second bay exists.

low/spec-deviation README.md:101 — tasks.md §4.6 names the prose "the docket is the branch" as falsified by this section, but that sentence is retained verbatim immediately above the new paragraph declaring "a docket in flight is a bay on disk" (:108). The two definitions now sit adjacent and disagree for a branch with no bay — exactly the case `next` answers with `no bay for X` → Reword :101 so the branch-level and fleet-level definitions read as one rule (e.g. the docket is the branch, and from outside it is the bay that branch has on disk).

results.title: new: the trunk-side entry point
results.summary: Added the trunk-side `new` verb: a `firstLeg` helper plus a `begin` handler in src/cli.js (registered as ['new', begin] since `new` is a reserved word), a USAGE row, and commands/new.md — the one command file declaring model/effort, pinned against bookings/ideation-ideate.md's parsed frontmatter. On the trunk `new` prints leg 1's waybill byte-identical to tests/golden/no-docket.txt; inside a bay it rebuilds leg 1 in cli.js (never touching src/inference.js), names the trunk in the header, warns on stdout via state.warnings, and still exits 0. npm test 368 pass / 0 fail (was 359), 432 TAP ok; all 14 machine-checkable contract criteria pass — the 2 remaining failures are Phase 5's gates and criterion 17 is Phase 6's judgment call. — Phase 4 (`new`) is implemented cleanly and matches the spec: the verb prints leg 1's waybill and exits 0, `tests/golden/no-docket.txt` is untouched and is now asserted at both renderer and CLI level, leg 1 is rebuilt inside `src/cli.js` rather than by widening `src/inference.js` (the change's zero-diff guardrail holds), the usage row aligns to the existing 18-column shape and satisfies the `^  (new|bay|next|status) ` acceptance grep, `['new', begin]` respects the reserved-word constraint, and `commands/new.md` inverts the no-model convention deliberately with the model/effort pinned against the parsed booking rather than against literals — including the `SlashCommand`/`Skill` declarations the context map flagged as the phase's likeliest silent failure. No critical or high findings: the six items are one documentation contradiction in the context map, one real but narrow booking-overlay inconsistency worth documenting, and four minor gaps. Ready to commit.
findings: medium/spec-deviation docs/ideation/new-bay-and-fleet/context-map.md:9 — The note asserts "Phases 1–3 are retained verbatim below", but the same diff deletes 136 lines from those sections, condensing the Phase 1/2/3 gate tables, Key Patterns and Dependencies and stripping the file:line evidence they recorded (e.g. `src/waybill.js:151` call-site lists, `tests/cli.test.js:208,224,236,259,267`). The map's own stated convention is "extended, not replaced" → restore the prior-phase sections byte-for-byte and append only the Phase 4 block, or reword the note to say prior phases were condensed and their line-level evidence dropped.

medium/spec-deviation src/cli.js:338 — `begin()` resolves bookings from `cwd`, so `new` run inside a bay (or in a repo carrying a `.waybill/bookings` overlay) prints leg 1 out of *that* overlay, while `commands/new.md`'s frontmatter is pinned to the shipped `bookings/ideation-ideate.md`. The spec requirement "`new` runs at the model and effort its booking names" then silently fails: the block can read `└ sonnet · low effort` while the session runs opus/high, with no test able to notice. `firstLeg`'s JSDoc claims the block belongs to the trunk, which makes the bay-overlay read doubly inconsistent → either resolve leg 1's booking from the main checkout rather than `cwd`, or state the limitation explicitly in `commands/new.md`'s model comment so the pin is not read as stronger than it is.

low/testing tests/cli.test.js:363 — The `waybill new` describe covers trunk, bay, multi-docket, bad option and no-repo, but not a detached HEAD, which is the one remaining shape of `docketOpen === false`: it falls through `firstLeg`'s passthrough and renders the bare `no docket open` with no branch and no warning, even though the operator is not on the trunk. `trunkName()` exists at `src/cli.js:73` precisely because that case bit the fleet header → add a case pinning the detached-HEAD output so the choice is recorded rather than incidental.

results.title: The session-facing branch
results.summary: Added the session-facing selection branch to commands/next.md — keyed on the exact SELECT A DOCKET: literal with verbatim staying the unconditional default — declared AskUserQuestion on its allowed-tools line, updated commands/status.md for the trunk fleet view, and pinned all of it in tests/commands.test.js by deriving the heading from renderSelect rather than repeating the literal. Resolved the design's self-contradiction on the re-run spelling toward node "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/src/cli.js" next <branch>, which is the only spelling the existing permission list actually covers, and widened the plugin-root sweep to cover the Task prose that now names it. — Phase 5 (tasks.md §6) is implemented faithfully and matches the spec's \"Verbatim rendering, with one keyed exception\" requirement: `commands/next.md` gains the `SELECT A DOCKET:`-keyed branch with `**verbatim**` surviving as the unconditional default, `AskUserQuestion` is on the `allowed-tools` line itself (acceptance criteria 13 and 14 both satisfied statically), and `commands/status.md` is updated for the trunk fleet view. The touched files are exactly the three the contract phase lists, no `src/` file was edited, and the two new tests are well-designed — the next.md literal is derived from `renderSelect` rather than re-typed, and `allowed-tools` is asserted through the frontmatter parser so prose cannot satisfy it. The widened `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` sweep is justified by the phase's own edge-case analysis (the new re-run line names the root outside a `!` line) and passes against every declared command file; the only real gap is that status.md's `DOCKETS:` literal got no equivalent pin. Ready to commit after the medium finding is weighed.

No current command file hits either case, so the widened sweep passes today → anchor on `line.trimStart().startsWith('<!--')` / `trimEnd().endsWith('-->')`, or note the limitation in the existing comment.

low/spec-deviation commands/status.md:20-22 — the frontmatter comment describes the trunk answer as "every effort in flight, one line per docket under `DOCKETS:`" with no empty-fleet caveat, while `renderFleet` (src/waybill.js:325-327) deliberately omits the `DOCKETS:` heading when nothing is open. The Task paragraph at :37-39 states it correctly, so the two halves of the same file disagree → add "or, with nothing open, the header line alone" to the comment.

low/spec-deviation commands/status.md:2 — the slash-command description now reads "or the whole fleet from the trunk" while `src/cli.js:22`'s USAGE row still reads "without the waybill"; the two user-facing descriptions of `status` no longer agree. The phase's context map (Phase 5 edge case 14) sanctions this because `src/cli.js` is out of this phase's file list and `tests/commands.test.js:374` pins the USAGE row byte-exact → leave as-is for this phase, but record it as a follow-up for the next change that legitimately opens `src/cli.js`.

results.title: Verification and the stderr finding
results.summary: Completed tasks.md §7: ran §7.1's verification (npm test 370 pass / 0 fail, 434 TAP ok, all six boundary git-diff checks green) and answered §7.2 with three live-session probes through the shipped `!` invocation — stderr IS captured and reaches the transcript labelled `[stderr]`, so `repoRoot`'s "is not inside a git repository" error was never invisible and the "captures stdout only" rationale in spec.md/src/cli.js/README.md is false; the probe also surfaced a new, material risk (a non-zero exit makes Claude Code report "Shell command failed for pattern" and never render the command file's `## Task`, so the trunk's exit-2 zero-docket and many-docket cases may never reach Phase 5's `SELECT A DOCKET:` branch), which is recorded in design.md as out-of-scope for the next change rather than fixed here. Both checkboxes ticked (28/28), `openspec validate --strict` valid, verify.mjs commits=6/6 pass=16 fail=0 judgment=1; no src/, tests/ or commands/ file was touched. — All three cycle-1 findings are fixed: design.md:63-73 now narrows the stderr conclusion to what was actually observed (non-zero exit surfaces stderr in the failure report) and explicitly says nothing here falsifies spec.md:47-48, src/cli.js:115-116 or README.md:142-143; tasks.md §7.2 gains the criterion-17 reconciliation paragraph; and both tasks.md:143 and the context map's Verification block now state the 46.5s/47.2s figures are two runs of one suite. I independently re-verified every mechanical claim in §7.1 against git — the eight in-a-bay goldens, no-docket.txt, src/inference.js and the six untouched modules are all `git diff --quiet`-clean against 08d0c6f, bay.txt is the only modified pre-existing golden with the other four goldens added new, and the `is not inside a git repository` literal appears zero times in this branch's src/cli.js diff — and confirmed the probe substitution's mechanics against the installed 0.3.1 `start()`. Three non-blocking findings remain, the substantive one being that design.md's new exit-contract risk bullet drops the "which stream / which trigger" hedge that tasks.md carries; the phase is markdown-only, accurate where it counts, and ready to commit.
findings: medium/logic openspec/changes/new-bay-and-fleet/design.md:75-80 — The new second Risks bullet repeats the hedge-dropping pattern cycle 1 flagged on the bullet above it, one axis over. It states unqualified that "when the `` ! `` line exits non-zero, Claude Code (2.1.267) reports a shell-command failure naming that line and never renders the file" and that "Both trunk cases that print and exit 2 are affected" — but the only probe behind it (tasks.md:200-205) wrote to **stderr** and exited 2, while the trunk cases write to **stdout**, and tasks.md:214-217 itself records that "whether the abort is triggered by the exit status, by the stream, or by both is unseparated" and that stdout preservation is "inferred from the `[stderr]` label, not observed". A design.md-only reader gets a settled fact where tasks.md carries a confounded inference. The direction of error is conservative (it over-files a risk rather than clearing one), which is why this is medium and not high. → Qualify the bullet to match tasks.md — e.g. "the one non-zero exit observed also wrote to stderr, so whether an exit-2 command whose output is on **stdout** loses its file is inferred, not measured; if it does, both trunk cases (§4.2) are affected" — or run the both-streams control the map's Phase 6 edge case 4 prescribes and state it on that evidence.

low/spec-deviation docs/ideation/new-bay-and-fleet/context-map.md:9 — The header asserts "Phases 1–5 are retained verbatim below", but the same diff rewrites Phase 5's Key Patterns, Dependencies, Conventions, all 20 Edge Cases and Risks into condensed one-liners and deletes the entire `## Verification (Phase 5)` bash block (old :353-378). The Phase 5 acceptance-gate commands and the re-run-spelling rationale are gone from the record. The prior committed phase (`405139b`) condensed Phase 4 the same way, so this is an inherited habit rather than a new regression — but the sentence claiming verbatim retention is false as written in a document whose stated convention is that every claim carries its reason. → Reword :9 to what actually happens ("earlier phases are retained in condensed form; only the current phase is at full detail"), or restore Phase 5's sections and condense nothing.

low/spec-deviation docs/ideation/new-bay-and-fleet/context-map.md:424 vs openspec/changes/new-bay-and-fleet/tasks.md:141 — The map's own Phase 6 risk bullet instructs: "if that cannot be done, say so plainly in `design.md` and `tasks.md` and leave 7.2 unticked rather than ticking it on inference." §7.2 is now ticked on a disclosed substitution (empty branch name standing in for the non-git cwd). The substitution's mechanics check out — verified against the installed 0.3.1 `start()`, whose arity check returns 2 after one `io.err` write before `repoRoot` and before `startBay` — and the reconciliation paragraph the cycle-1 finding asked for is present, so the tick is defensible; but the map and tasks.md now read as contradicting each other on the same page of the same diff. → Add a clause to the map's risk bullet recording which route was taken and why ("closed on a disclosed observable-equivalent substitution, reconciled at tasks.md §7.2; the literal route stays open"), so the two documents agree.
